candidates.name: .NET Mutex
verified_facts: Mutex grants exclusive access to a shared resource and supports named cross-process synchronization
WaitOne can request ownership with a bounded timeout and ReleaseMutex releases ownership
semantic_limits: A mutex alone does not prove the owner is the canonical runner or that protected files are consistent after an abandoned mutex

candidates.name: .NET Mutex.OpenExisting
verified_facts: OpenExisting opens a specified named mutex when it already exists
Global and Local prefixes select machine-wide or session-wide namespaces on Windows
semantic_limits: Opening a mutex does not request ownership and an access failure must not be treated as absence

candidates.name: .NET MutexAcl.OpenExisting
verified_facts: MutexAcl.OpenExisting opens an existing named mutex with requested rights
Global names are machine-wide while Local or unprefixed names are session-wide
semantic_limits: Successful open proves only accessible mutex presence, not canonical process identity or liveness

candidates.name: .NET EventWaitHandle.OpenExisting
verified_facts: OpenExisting opens a named synchronization event if it exists
Named synchronization objects can be used for cross-process state signalling
semantic_limits: An event signal is advisory state and cannot replace process, task, receipt, and Git readback

candidates.name: .NET FileStream
verified_facts: FileStream supports file I/O, explicit sharing modes, flushing, locking, and safe disposal
Lock prevents other processes from reading or writing a selected file region
semantic_limits: File locks can be released on close or process exit and do not identify the locking process by themselves

candidates.name: .NET FileStream constructor
verified_facts: FileStream constructors accept FileMode, FileAccess, FileShare, buffer size, and FileOptions
FileShare.None requests no sharing by other file streams
semantic_limits: An exclusive open can fail for permissions, path, or unrelated locks; failure is not proof of a live canonical owner

candidates.name: .NET FileStreamOptions
verified_facts: FileStreamOptions groups access, mode, sharing, options, buffer size, and preallocation settings
The configured access determines CanRead and CanWrite behavior
semantic_limits: Recorded options do not prove the operating system honored durability or that later readers saw the same bytes

candidates.name: .NET FileStreamOptions.Share
verified_facts: Share determines how the file can be shared by processes
Sharing policy is a bitwise combination of FileShare values
semantic_limits: A permissive share mode cannot serve as a single-owner lock and a restrictive mode still needs owner correlation

candidates.name: .NET FileOptions
verified_facts: FileOptions contains advanced stream options including WriteThrough
WriteThrough requests writes through intermediate cache directly toward disk
semantic_limits: WriteThrough does not replace Flush, close, hash readback, or storage-health verification

candidates.name: .NET FileStream.Flush
verified_facts: Flush clears stream buffers and writes buffered data to the file
Flush(true) also requests clearing intermediate file buffers to disk
semantic_limits: A completed flush does not prove later Git publication, remote durability, or semantic receipt validity

candidates.name: .NET FileStream Unix lock behavior
verified_facts: FileStream.Lock behavior on Unix depends on file access and .NET version
Starting in .NET 6 read-only streams use a shared read lock on Unix
semantic_limits: Windows F-host validation must record platform and runtime; Unix lock behavior must not be assumed on Windows

candidates.name: .NET File.Replace
verified_facts: File.Replace replaces destination content with another file and can create a backup
Replacement can report path, permission, read-only, or merge errors
semantic_limits: Replacement success must be followed by length, hash, JSON, and Git readback; backup existence alone is insufficient

candidates.name: .NET File.ReadAllBytes
verified_facts: ReadAllBytes opens a file, reads its full contents into a byte array, and closes it
It reports invalid path, directory, access, or I/O failures
semantic_limits: Reading bytes proves only the observed file contents at that instant, not producer identity or remote publication

candidates.name: .NET File.WriteAllBytes
verified_facts: WriteAllBytes creates or overwrites a file with the supplied byte array and closes it
An existing target is truncated and overwritten
semantic_limits: Direct overwrite is not an atomic publication protocol and must not be used without staging, flush, and readback

candidates.name: .NET FileInfo
verified_facts: FileInfo exposes length, timestamps, attributes, full path, and link target metadata
FileInfo can refresh cached filesystem information
semantic_limits: Metadata can change between reads and does not substitute for full-byte hashing or JSON schema validation

candidates.name: .NET FileSystemInfo.LinkTarget
verified_facts: LinkTarget returns the target path for a filesystem link or null for a non-link
Symbolic links and junctions are link types addressed by related resolution APIs
semantic_limits: A textual link target can be relative and must be resolved before containment or ownership decisions
